name: Aiptasia pallida
relation: new combination in *Exaiptasia*, then junior subjective synonym of *E. diaphana*
evidence: WoRMS unaccept reason: new genus created by Grajales & Rodriguez 2014 (the genus step). The synonymy with diaphana is a taxonomic judgement; Opinion 2404 (2017) declined to give pallida precedence over diaphana and Opinion 2500 (2023) declined to reverse it. They fix the name only if the two are conspecific. The article uses a worldwide sensu lato concept (source p. 17).

name: Exaiptasia pallida
relation: junior subjective synonym of *E. diaphana*; precedence of *diaphana* upheld
evidence: WoRMS record (modified 2020-12-16) still reads 'pallida valid until ICZN rules Case 3790', which predates Opinion 2500 (2023); the record is stale. In February 2016 Case 3633 was pending.

name: Anthopleura cascaia
relation: nomen nudum (unavailable name); WoRMS links it to a species described in 2025
evidence: ICZN Art. 11.1: no description. The link from the nomen nudum to Anthopleura correae is made in Durán-Fuentes et al. (2025), whose authors include the source article's first author; the present author is not an author of it. A nomen nudum has no status, so the link is a concept-level judgement, not a synonymy.

name: Bunodosoma cavernata
relation: gender agreement of the epithet (ICZN Art. 34.2)

name: Corynactis caribbeorum
evidence: Original combination Pseudocorynactis caribbeorum den Hartog, 1980 (WoRMS authority without parentheses). Fautin (2011) sank Pseudocorynactis into Corynactis; Ocaña et al. (2017) restored it. The article followed Fautin (2011) and recorded the alternative (source pp. 21, 24): not a lag.

name: Epizoanthus cutressi
evidence: WoRMS cites Swain et al. (2015) as the new-combination reference, but that paper is a study of polyp retraction musculature, not the act; the act transferring cutressi to Bergia is not identified here.

name: Haliplanella luciae
evidence: WoRMS cites no act; whether the synonymy is objective or subjective is not recorded.

name: Isaurus duchassaingi

name: Lebrunia danae

name: Parazoanthus puertoricense
